_note: LA PROGRESIÓN — what the tutorial teaches and in what order, which barrios are open, and what each mode starts with. `tutorial.js`, `progress.js` and `modes.js` keep the state machine and the persistence; this is the shape of the journey.
_scope: The steps and their thresholds are content — 'drive 260 px and turn 1.6 radians' is a judgement about when somebody has understood steering. Reading the input, accumulating the distance and writing localStorage are not.

tutorial._note: A guided, TIMERLESS run that teaches every control and then the whole delivery loop. Six steps teach, the seventh congratulates and ends the run as a win.
tutorial._keys: `key` is the i18n key of the instruction. Four of them end in `.touch`/`.keys` — the HUD picks the wording from the pointer type, because 'hold the rim' and 'hold X' are the same lesson and a phone must not be told about a keyboard.
tutorial._gates: `gate` names the CONDITION the engine implements; the numbers beside it are this file's. A gate with no implementation is a step nobody can pass, which is why `tests/test_progression.py` checks every one against the module.

steps.note: moving is not the lesson — TURNING is, so it asks for both

steps.speedNote: scaled by tuning.speed, so the lesson still passes for a player who has slowed the game down

steps.note: at speed, or holding the brake while parked would teach nothing
the run ends as a WIN, so the results screen says so

tutorial.soundNote: played on every advance — the same three notes a perfect delivery gets, so progress feels like the thing the game already rewards

unlocks._note: Which districts a new save starts with, and which are closed for the MVP.
unlocks._mvpNote: A SCOPE DECISION, NOT A GEOMETRY ONE. Reopening a barrio is deleting it from this list — the wall, the stage cards and the delivery clamp all follow from it.
unlocks._shapeNote: The gate is the BARRIOS THEMSELVES and not a line, because in a 2-D world a line is the wrong shape: the four inland ones OVERLAP the coastal districts on x (Chacarita starts at 28642, a third of the way into El Cocal), so a single wall fenced off exactly the three districts that are supposed to be open.
unlocks._graph: The unlock GRAPH is not here: a stage names the district it opens (`unlock` in content/world/stages.json), so there is one place a stage's reward is written and it sits with the stage.

modes._note: What each mode starts with. Durations live in `src/game/timers.js` — they are seconds, and the untimed modes carry no clock at all rather than a large number nobody counts down.

arcade.note: ARCADE PICKS ITS SKY. Three minutes is shorter than any phase of the day, so a cycle would either never turn or strobe. `cycle` is offered for anyone who wants the turn.

explore.note: RECORRER GETS A DAY. Ten real minutes for a full turn — sunny, atardecer, night, amanecer — with a storm rolling in now and then and handing the sky back where it left off. An explicit `weather` still wins: asking for one and getting a cycle would be a bug.

story.note: A stage's sky is part of its brief. Except la Travesía, whose sky and tide ARE the brief: it rotates through four conditions by ATTEMPT rather than naming one, so the estero is a different course at bajamar than at pleamar.

tutorial.note: Nothing to learn from a storm on your first run.
